says.placement_reason: The printed count 8 and R115,5 center-to-hole radius, together with the centered circular layout showing holes on both cardinal axes and between them, establish an equally distributed circular pattern using 360/count. The pattern center is the ring origin; the rightmost hole anchors the pattern on +X. Solid concentric circles in the main face-on view show the countersink openings on the visible top face.

sources.note: The linked callout specifies eight Ø3,4 THRU ALL holes with Ø6,9 X 90° countersinks. The solid visible concentric hole edges establish top openings. R115,5 and the clear axis-aligned circular layout support the stated pattern. The countersink geometry fits both retained thickness readings. Verification: The callout '8 x Ø 3,4 THRU ALL' with the countersink symbol 'Ø 6,9 X 90°' gives the hole size, through condition, and countersink. The main view shows 8 holes on the dash-dot pitch circle: one on each cardinal axis (0/90/180/270°) and one on each diagonal. That matches an even 360/8 = 45° spacing, and a start angle of 0 at the rightmost (+X) hole is valid. The R115,5 leader runs from the ring centre to the lower-left hole centre, so it gives the pitch radius. The doubled circles at each hole are drawn solid in the face-on (+Z) view, so the countersinks open on the top face. Derived countersink depth is (6,9−3,4)/2 = 1,75, which is less than both 2,0 and 3,0, so the countersink is valid for both thickness readings.

sources.note: The dimensioned annulus and edge-view thickness readings meet the permitted flat-ring template. The stacked thickness ambiguity is preserved under the possible-reading contract and does not block eligibility. Verification: Original D-025 page 1 shows a face-on annulus. The outer diameter is dimensioned Ø250,0 ±0,2 (D-025/drawing/n/250.0@1-1) and the inner diameter Ø224,0 +0,3/0,0 (D-025/drawing/n/224.0@1-1). The ±0,2, +0,3 and 0,0 values are tolerances, not separate geometry. The left edge view is a plain constant-width strip. Its thickness leader prints the stacked readings 3,0 (D-025/drawing/n/3.0@1-1) and 2,0 (D-025/drawing/n/2.0@1-1), and the units note says millimetres (D-025/drawing/general/units). Under the possible-reading contract, these are kept as unselected constant-thickness options. The face view shows 8 equally spaced holes on the R115,5 centreline circle (D-025/drawing/callout/p1-3) at the cardinal and diagonal positions. They carry the callout '8 x Ø 3,4 THRU ALL' with countersink 'Ø 6,9 X 90°' (D-025/drawing/callout/p1-1 and p1-2). The resulting countersink depth, (6,9-3,4)/2 = 1,75, is valid for both the 2,0 and 3,0 readings. The outline has no notches, lobes, steps or other unsupported contour. The only general unmodeled detail is the unspecified edge break, DEBURR AND BREAK SHARP EDGES (D-025/drawing/general/edge_finish), and the proposal correctly lists it as an omitted minor detail. supported=true, constant_thickness=true, outline_exact=true and an empty essential_uncertainty are therefore supported. Accepting this eligibility does not approve the countersink opening face or the feature completeness; those are separate keys.

display.message: Waiting for review: needs_input. The proposal's value is unknown/null, and the protocol requires needs_input for that. The original evidence also leaves the match open. The drawing's title (D-025/drawing/title) is "Bygge Base Ring" and its section is "Z-axis". No BOM row uses that exact name, and no row is in a "Z-axis" section. The material is "3.3315 (EN-AW 5005)" (D-025/drawing/material) and the notes say "Aluminium" (D-025/drawing/notes). Several rows list Aluminium and have a similar name: BOM:build-plate/build-base ("Build base"), BOM:build-plate/build-cylinder-clamp-ring ("Build cylinder clamp ring") and BOM:build-plate/seal-clamp-plate. All of these are in the "Build-plate" section and have no datasheet that links to ByggeBaseRing_Version2.PDF. Choosing between them would mean reading 'Bygge' as 'build' and treating the different names and sections as equivalent. The task says not to assume that. The proposal's unknown state and its explanation of the ambiguity are consistent with the evidence. The cited fact IDs exist in the original evidence. Resolving the link needs a human mapping decision or new evidence, such as a datasheet link or a confirmed section mapping.
